common_name: Else Poulsen Rose (Historic Pink Floribunda, Mother of the Class)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Else Poulsen, introduced in Denmark in 1924, is one of the foundational roses of the entire floribunda class.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Else Poulsen, bred by Svend Poulsen in Denmark and introduced in 1924, bears large clusters of semi-double, bright rose-pink flowers with a light fragrance, and is historically significant as one of the earliest and most influential roses in developing the modern floribunda class through the Poulsen family's hybridizing program crossing polyanthas with hybrid teas. Its vigorous, healthy, heavily blooming habit set the template that later floribundas would follow, and it remains available today as a piece of living rose-breeding history. It reblooms reliably through the growing season with good disease resistance for its age. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom, and prune moderately in late winter to shape the plant.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame
